transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having a hard time since we got a new operations manager. He’s been picking apart inspection procedures I’ve used for years, and I can’t seem to shut it off when I get home. I’m wound up, I snap at my husband, and I lie awake replaying meetings. Then at work I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble.
When exactly did these symptoms—feeling wound up, snapping at your husband, replaying meetings—first start in relation to when the new operations manager began?

I was doing fine before he came in. Once he started changing the procedures, it built up within a few weeks. By about the second month, I could tell it was following me home and affecting more than just work.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things in your life—like your health, finances, or family—that have nothing to do with your job situation?
No, not really. It’s mostly tied to what’s going on at work.
Besides feeling anxious and wound up, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
I haven’t really noticed feeling sad or losing interest in things. It’s more that I’m keyed up about work.
Have you noticed yourself feeling hopeless, tearful, or overly critical of yourself since this all started?
No, I haven’t really felt hopeless or tearful. I don’t think I’ve been putting myself down much either—it’s more frustration about the work situation.
Would you say your predominant feeling has been anxiety and being keyed up, or do you notice a mix of both low mood and anxiety together?

It’s mainly anxiety, being keyed up. Since the new manager started questioning the procedures I’ve used for years, I keep replaying things and second-guessing myself. I don’t feel low exactly—just tense and frustrated.
